I've been farming this 1.5 mu for 20 years now, same as my father did before me. It's small, but it's what I have, and I know every corner of it. My wheat and maize take turns — wheat goes in around October, comes off in early June, and maize goes in that same week, off before October. That's how everyone around here does it, and I don't mess with what works.

For the wheat this year, I'm planting the same improved variety I used last year — I bought the seed from the shop in town, 25 jin per mu, same as always. That means about 37 or 38 jin total for my 1.5 mu. For fertilizer, I put base fertilizer before sowing: I buy two 50kg bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) from the dealer, that's 100kg total, spread across the 1.5 mu. Then topdressing — I topdress twice with urea. First time at green-up, I use about 15kg urea per mu. Second time at jointing, another 15kg per mu. So that's roughly 16kg nitrogen per mu when you count the base. Phosphorus and potassium come from the compound fertilizer, about 6kg P and 4kg K per mu. I won't skip the K entirely because last year my neighbor Wang did, and his wheat lodged worse than mine.

I irrigate three times for wheat: once before winter to help it survive, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. The well water costs electricity, but if it doesn't rain, I have no choice. I spray herbicide once after sowing, and one fungicide at heading because the rust came through two years ago and I lost yield.

For the summer maize, I plant hybrid seed — everyone uses hybrid now, you can't get good yield without it. I plant about 3 jin per mu, so 4.5 jin total. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing, about 40kg per mu, then topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage, about 20kg urea per mu. That works out to roughly 16kg N, 5kg P, and 4kg K per mu. I don't till the maize — I use the no-till planter right after the wheat combine leaves the field. Time is short in summer, and the soil is already loose enough.

I irrigate maize twice: once at seedling if it's dry, and once at filling. Two sprays: herbicide at 3-5 leaves, and one insecticide because the corn borer always comes.

My household has six mouths, and my wife and I do most of the field work ourselves. Two of my family work in the city and send some money back, which helps pay for inputs. But I still watch every yuan — a bag of urea is real money. Still, I'd rather put a bit too much fertilizer than risk an empty harvest. A bad year means borrowing money; wasting a few jin of fertilizer just means eating a little less pork.

I expect about 550kg of wheat per mu and 600kg of maize per mu if the weather cooperates. That's what I got last year, and the year before was similar.
